name: Geller Voiding Trial
question: How do retrograde-fill and spontaneous voiding trials compare in detecting prolonged postoperative voiding dysfunction after female pelvic floor surgery?

design.population: 50 women undergoing surgery for urinary incontinence, pelvic organ prolapse, or both between November 2009 and March 2010.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Methods and Results; PubMed affiliation

verdictNote: Retrograde testing was more specific; the abstract gives no prespecified accuracy threshold.
takeaway: In 50 women receiving both postoperative tests, retrograde-fill voiding trials had 94.4% sensitivity and 58.1% specificity for voiding dysfunction lasting at least 7 days, versus 100% and 25.8% with spontaneous trials; retrograde testing failed fewer women (62% versus 84%).

reports.label: Randomized-order diagnostic report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed and Crossref list September 2011, without a day
reports.citation: Geller EJ, Hankins KJ, Parnell BA, et al. "Diagnostic accuracy of retrograde and spontaneous voiding trials for postoperative voiding dysfunction: a randomized controlled trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2011;118(3):637-642. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e318229e8dd
reports.followUp: Voiding dysfunction lasting at least 7 days was the diagnostic reference outcome

results.measure: Sensitivity and specificity for voiding dysfunction lasting at least 7 days
results.note: The abstract does not state a prespecified diagnostic-accuracy threshold or denominators for the estimates.

results.measure: Failure rate for each test across the paired cohort
results.note: Each woman underwent both tests; these are test-level failure rates, not randomized-group rates. Numerators are not provided in the abstract.

results.measure: Positive and negative predictive values for voiding dysfunction lasting at least 7 days
results.note: The abstract does not provide the underlying two-by-two tables.

results.measure: Preferred voiding trial, irrespective of test order
results.note: Preference denominator and the remainder of responses are not given in the abstract.

harms.label: Duration of postoperative retention by paired-test failure pattern
harms.note: Women failing both tests had 12.6 ± 14.4 days of retention versus 2.5 ± 2.1 days among those failing only one test (P = .004); group denominators were not reported in the abstract.

delivery.label: Paired testing and randomized order
delivery.value: All 50 women received both methods; 25 were randomized to retrograde first and 25 to spontaneous first.
